title: Values of heap gates
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers with $k\le n$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and let $bj,o,L$ be natural numbers with $o+L\le n$. Suppose that for every $q$ with $1\le q<2^{L+1}$, the gate at position $bj+(q-1)$ is the heap gate with parameters $n$, base $n+bj$, offset $o$, and index $q$. Also suppose $bj+(2^{L+1}-1)\le\mathrm{total}(n,k)$. Then for every $q$ with $1\le q<2^{L+1}$, the value at vertex $n+bj+(q-1)$ is true exactly when the heap path of $x$ from offset $o$ at depth $\lfloor\log_2 q\rfloor$ equals $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$-bit inputs
